2.text: 9. INCANTATIONS TO BRING BACK THE DYING.
2.note: mz/ocr misread as DVING (V for small-cap Y); raster clearly reads DYING.

3.text: (a) When a man has just died, and the body is lying in the inner

4.text: room, another person leaves the house, goes into the wilderness, and talks

5.text: to the Upper Being, to the Morning-Dawn. He says, “My mind is uncertain.

6.text: Enough (stop doubting). Whom else may I ask for help? You are the fittest.

7.text: Oh! give me your dog. I will also use it as a dog for myself. I am

8.text: sorrowful for my child; it is gone away to a far-off place. Therefore let me

9.text: use that dog for my assistant.” He makes a motion with his left hand, as
9.note: closing quote curly per §1/§5.6; mz text carries a straight quote artifact.

10.text: if receiving the dog from somewhere. Then he comes back and blows into

11.text: the ear of the dead person, and howls like a dog, “Uu, uu, uu!” Then

12.text: this dog starts on, pursuing the dead man. It follows him, barking and

13.text: howling, “Haw, haw, haw!” Soon it passes ahead of him, and meets him
13.note: a small ring-shaped ink mark sits above this line, over 'meets'; not part of any letter, ruled not-type (blot/offset ink).

14.text: on the road with fierce barking. It snaps at him, and intercepts his way in

15.text: every direction. At last it makes him come back from his long journey.

16.text: Then he must enter the body and put it on again. After that he begins to

17.text: breathe, and gradually improves, and finally he, though dead, revives again.

18.text: Told by Rɪkeˊwg̣ɪ (man) at Mariinsky Post, 1900.
18.resolved: Rɪ = R + U+026A; keˊwg̣ɪ = k, e + U+02CA, w, g + U+0323, U+026A
18.note: personal name; g dotted below (U+0323) confirmed at 4x, ɪ is the bare-stem small-cap sort not plain i.

19.text: (b) If I want to retard one going away, I will transform, of my five

20.text: fingers, the little one into the dying man, and hold it tightly in my palm.

21.text: When he walks onward, I will intercept his way. I will bark like a dog,
21.note: a tiny raised speck sits between 'I' and 'will' (first occurrence); too small and straight to be the printed apostrophe/stress shape seen elsewhere on this page, ruled a fleck of ink rather than a mark.

22.text: and make him come back. I will make his soul into a drifted tree; I will

23.text: blow as a high wind, and I will call it to the shore; I will draw it with my

24.text: breath toward the land: “Kamo, kamo, kamo, kamo!” I will catch the tree

25.text: by its roots, and draw it to the shore.

26.text: Told by Kamenvaˊt, a Reindeer Chukchee, man, in the Kolyma Country, 1897.

27.text: (c) When a man suffering from disease becomes quite weak, and is about

28.text: to die, he is carried out of the house, and his body is rubbed over with

29.text: something, for instance, with snow. Then another man talks to the Upper

30.text: Regions. He calls to the Pebbly River, and speaks thus: “O Pebbly River,
30.note: thin space before colon in print (French spacing) collapsed per §2.9; closing quote curly per §1/§5.6.

31.text: come down! I will use you for my assistant!” At the same time he calls

32.text: also the East Wind. Then comes a great fall of rain. The river is greatly

33.text: swollen. The patient becomes the rapids of the stream; everything is carried

34.text: away. He becomes quite clean, and the water takes with it all rubbish.

35.text: Then the sufferer becomes better, and is carried back into the house.

36.text: Told by Rɪkeˊwg̣ɪ (man) at Mariinsky Post, 1900.
36.resolved: Rɪ = R + U+026A; keˊwg̣ɪ = k, e + U+02CA, w, g + U+0323, U+026A
36.note: same personal name as line 18, g dotted below confirmed at 4x.

37.resolved: Oiwa = O, i, w, a + U+02CA (stress); cirg with caron on c (U+010D / c+U+030C) and dot below on g (U+0323); Ê = U+00CA (E with circumflex) + stress (U+02CA); wgan with dot below on g (U+0323)
37.note: hyphenated compound name, one stress mark per element; both g's dotted below confirmed at 4x.

38.text: To whatsoever person has incurred my anger, I say, “You are not a

39.text: man! you are an old seal-skin!” I call the shrimps from the sea. “O Shrimps!
